acceptance_criteria.criterion: Railway can build and start the existing trusted issuer edge from repository-owned configuration.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: railway.toml (repository-owned) sets [build] builder = "RAILPACK" and [deploy] startCommand to the unmodified scripts/hunter_issue_agent_issuer.py entrypoint with --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT and the repository-owned production provenance resolver, plus a /healthz healthcheck. The issuer edge itself is untouched; only repo-owned config and the resolver seam were added. A live Railway start requires the operator variables/volume and is tracked by #423/#390, but the deterministic start command and build definition are present in the candidate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Startup fails closed when required authority/configuration is absent or malformed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: test_production_resolver_missing_environment_fails_closed pins that a provenance resolver with missing environment fails closed; test_missing_provenance_tables_fail_closed pins that absent provenance tables are not degraded; test_view_with_wrong_verification_key_fails_closed pins that key material not pinned to the operator root fails; and the issuer's own test_missing_operational_configuration_fails_closed (unchanged, exercised in the related suite) pins transport startup fail-closed behaviour.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Production provenance resolution is deterministic and authority-bound.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: production_provenance_resolver builds a read-only SourceHandlingProvenanceView once from the operator environment and resolves the last strict-known record at the given cutoff: every row carries a SHA-256 record identity, an Ed25519 signature over the canonical claims, an explicit kind shape, and canonical timestamps; history commitments (single genesis, linear supersession, strictly advancing known_at, signed/revisioned head) are re-derived from stored rows, never from process state. test_resolve_and_unknown_identities, test_full_authority_publication_with_real_production_resolver and test_production_resolver_resolves_from_environment pin deterministic authority-bound resolution.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Evidence/replay SQLite lives on a documented Railway Volume path.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: railway.toml and docs/ISSUE_AGENT_ISSUER_DEPLOYMENT.md "Option 3: Railway" document the Volume mount at /data with HUNTER_ISSUE_AGENT_EVIDENCE_DB=/data/evidence.sqlite; the doc states the Railway filesystem outside an attached Volume is not authoritative persistent storage and that the canonical Evidence/replay DB must live on the mounted Volume. The provenance writer/view resolve the exact database path (single source of truth HUNTER_ISSUE_AGENT_EVIDENCE_DB), so both authority and replay state live on the volume.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: /healthz can become healthy on the deployed service once operator secrets/config are present.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The unmodified issuer edge serves /healthz (healthz path in scripts/hunter_issue_agent_issuer.py) and railway.toml wires healthcheckPath = "/healthz" with a 120s timeout. Live health on the deployed Railway service cannot be demonstrated from committed content in this slice: it requires the operator-entered variables and volume creation, which are outstanding steps tracked by #423/#390.

defect_families.evidence: Every timestamp that reaches admission, ordering or cutoff is derived from the operator-owned clock: _next_admission_time = max(clock.now(), MAX(admission_time) + 1µs) with _aware_utc, and a caller or payload contributes no time. Cutoff resolution trusts only the operator-provisioned effective_from/recorded_at/known_at/admission_time, each round-tripped through canonical _time_text. test_conflicting_same_known_at_rejected_at_write and test_backdated_known_at_is_not_admitted_until_admission pin the ordering and admission boundaries.

One real BEGIN IMMEDIATE spans the whole protected sequence: read operator root -> verify root -> read current head -> validate predecessor/revision -> insert record -> update head -> commit. Schema initialization now runs once in _initialize() on its own connection before the write transaction, so the implicit commit inside executescript can no longer release the write lock mid-sequence. test_write_lock_is_held_for_the_entire_protected_sequence holds a writer transaction open and proves a second independent repository instance cannot interleave until it commits, and test_competing_corrections_from_same_predecessor_cannot_branch races two independent instances against a shared genesis and proves at most one direct successor is admitted with a linear revisioned head.

A record identity is SHA-256 over the canonical claims EXCLUDING supersedes_record_id, so re-recording identical current-head content is the same identity (idempotent by construction) while any distinct correction yields a distinct identity; the heads table keys on (provenance_id, provenance_kind) with a UNIQUE current_record_id so an identity is current for at most one lineage. test_record_resolve_and_unknown_identities and the idempotent re-record path pin identity semantics.

Every absent/unknown branch fails closed: missing provenance tables raise SourceHandlingBlockedError (test_missing_provenance_tables_fail_closed); unknown identity returns None only when genuinely unresolved (otherwise 'provenance history is not completely knowable at cutoff'); wrong verification key or unverifiable signature raises (test_view_with_wrong_verification_key_fails_closed, tamper tests); missing/malformed environment fails closed (test_production_resolver_missing_environment_fails_closed); unknown provenance_kind is rejected by the column CHECK. The concurrency fix preserves this: a blocked or rejected competitor surfaces SourceHandlingBlockedError, never an out-of-band state.

Provenance is persisted in dedicated append-only tables (UPDATE/DELETE triggers on the record table, delete-blocking trigger on the heads table), never a nested or attached metadata surface, and only in the exact Evidence Intelligence database named by HUNTER_ISSUE_AGENT_EVIDENCE_DB whose path is documented on the Railway volume. No ephemeral filesystem assumption is introduced; the issuer's existing persistence for the canonical build, authorization receipt and replay state is unchanged.

Admission_time is repository-wide monotonic (MAX+1µs with a frozen-clock-safe max), revision strictly increases per lineage, known_at strictly increases along the chain, and every invariant is re-derived from stored rows on each read (_validate_chain) rather than from process or clock state, so restart cannot perturb any ordering guarantee. The concurrency tests also assert head revision equals record count after a multi-writer race, pinning restart/ordering behaviour under contention.

This range does not touch the connectors, .githooks, .github/workflows or the .hunter channel governing authorization identity: the issuer's existing replay protection (test_replay_after_process_restart_does_not_execute_again), repository/owner binding, and authorization verification are exercised by the unchanged related suite, and the new resolver/writer introduce no capability to re-aim or replay an authorization -- resolve is deterministic and read-only, and the writer is operator-owned, never run in the issuer runtime.

This review is the pre-ready hostile-review attestation: it is recorded against the exact 36f3b5826..HEAD content (blob SHAs and review_target_digest re-derived by the script), covers all applicable families (DFF-001..007, DFF-013), all adversarial dimensions, and the governing Issue #426's acceptance criteria, and carries no unresolved blocking finding as recorded here.

findings.evidence: Identity was initially defined over a payload that included supersedes_record_id, making an idempotent re-record of unchanged current-head content produce a new record_id and therefore be misread as a different identity or as a rejected correction. Resolved by defining record_id = SHA-256 over the canonical claims EXCLUDING supersedes_record_id, so re-recording identical content is the same identity while supersession stays bound by the signed claims and linear-chain validation. Pinned by the idempotent re-record path and test_schema_is_idempotent_across_repository_instances.

The strictly-later recommended known_at check ran before the idempotent short-circuit, so a writer re-recording unchanged current-head content was rejected as backdated. Resolved by returning the idempotent identity before enforcing the strictly-later correction rule, and by storing the boosted head_known_at used by both paths in one place. Pinned by test_conflicting_same_known_at_rejected_at_write, test_backdated_known_at_is_not_admitted_until_admission and the idempotent re-record tests.

Live Railway operational proof remains outstanding: operator-entered variables (verification key, key SHA-256, genesis rule SHA-256, automation signing/verifying keys, authorization verifying key, repository/owner/execution-branch variables), creation of the /data Volume, and setting HUNTER_ISSUE_AGENT_WEBHOOK_URL from the real deployed HTTPS domain are operator steps, and a live authorized Issue event passing end-to-end against the deployed service has not been demonstrated. #423 and #390 remain open pending that proof; nothing in this range closes them.

Independent review found that _transaction() ran connection.executescript(_SCHEMA) inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE: under legacy transaction control executescript implicitly commits a pending transaction, releasing the intended write lock before record_provenance read the current head, so two independent writers could race from the same current_record_id and admit different successors. Resolved by moving schema initialization to _initialize(), an idempotent step on its own connection before the protected transaction begins, so BEGIN IMMEDIATE now remains active for the entire read->verify->validate->insert->update->commit sequence. Pinned by test_write_lock_is_held_for_the_entire_protected_sequence (deterministically fails on the previous build) and test_competing_corrections_from_same_predecessor_cannot_branch (end-to-end linearity under a two-writer race).
